entities.summary:
Luis Julian de Milà y de Borja was a cardinal of the Catholic Church who played a pivotal role in shaping the Counter-Reformation during the tumultuous early 16th century. Born into the powerful Della Rovere family, he rose through the ranks to become Pope Julius II's close confidant and chief advisor.

As a key figure in the papacy, de Milà y de Borja orchestrated the execution of heretics, promoted the arts, and expanded the Church's influence across Europe. His tenure as cardinal coincided with significant events such as the Sack of Rome in 1527 and the Protestant Reformation's early stages.

De Milà y de Borja's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped establish the Jesuits and influenced the development of Catholic dogma during the Council of Trent. His impact on the Church's stance on faith, art, and governance left a lasting impression on Western history.

The cardinal's remarkable life was marked by both incredible achievements and personal struggles. Despite his formidable position, de Milà y de Borja struggled with depression and faced opposition from within the Church due to his perceived nepotism and favoritism towards certain factions.

entities.summary:
Luis Julian de Milà y de Borja was a cardinal of the Catholic Church. Born in Xàtiva, Spain in 1432 and ordained as a priest by Pope Eugenius IV in 1455, he rose through the ranks to become a cardinal in 1483. He played a key role in the papal elections of 1492, where he supported the election of Pope Alexander VI's daughter, Lucrezia Borgia. De Milà was also a diplomat and served as ambassador to Spain for Pope Pius III in 1504.

As cardinal, de Milà participated in several important events, including the Council of Trent (1545-1563), where he contributed to the reform of the Catholic Church. He died in 1510, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most influential cardinals of his time.

His actions had significant consequences, shaping the course of European politics and religion during the Renaissance. His influence can still be seen in the modern-day Catholic Church, with many of his reforms remaining in place today.

In terms of cultural impact, de Milà's diplomatic career helped to establish Spain as a major player in European affairs, paving the way for future Spanish conquests. His involvement in the papal elections also cemented the Borgia family's grip on power, leaving a lasting legacy in Italian politics.
